source.title: PEAK: Precise and Persistent Concept Erasure via k-Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Man Jiang; Ouxiang Li; Wei Xue; Zhen-Hua Tang; Yuan Wang; Shuo Wang; Yan-Bin Hao

record.tranche_reason: The study uses k-sparse autoencoder features as units for locating and suppressing concepts in diffusion-model activations, but does not test the claim's neuron-pole job shares or the listed language-model interpretability claims.
record.gate_note: The reported evidence concerns kSAE features in text-to-image diffusion models, not individual language-model neurons or explanations tested on held-out activations. The paper reports feature discrimination and feature interventions; these findings do not test any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study trains k-sparse autoencoders on Stable Diffusion cross-attention activations and uses selected SAE features to erase concepts. It reports its own method's erasure and preservation performance. It does not audit the job shares of neurons or neuron poles, does not test neuron explanations on held-out activations, does not build neuron-based attribution graphs, and works on SAE features in diffusion models rather than raw language-model neurons. None of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that PEAK's kSAE-guided feature localization and parameter fine-tuning erase target concepts (nudity, objects, styles) while preserving unrelated semantics and generation quality. They also report robustness to adversarial recovery attacks and generalization across diffusion architectures.
record.recipe_differences: Uses kSAEs on internal diffusion-model activations to localize and erase visual concepts; it does not perform the original language-model neuron-pole audit or test neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that selected feature groups control different nudity attributes; feature-selection criteria and preservation weight also affect erasure and preservation outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected SAE features in Stable Diffusion v1.4 keep a mean directional ROC-AUC above 0.8 for nudity versus matched non-nudity prompts across denoising timesteps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastively selected SAE features in diffusion models carry concept-discriminative signal across denoising steps.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing SAE feature groups associated with armpit, belly and breast attributes cuts the matching NudeNet detections by 94, 95 and 276. Zeroing all of them jointly leaves 4, 1 and 2 detections.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Localized SAE features in diffusion models give attribute-specific causal control over generated content.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the relevant feature results. The quantitative feature-intervention evidence is from Stable Diffusion v1.4; additional architecture results are described qualitatively. These findings concern diffusion-model SAE features, not language-model neurons or held-out explanation prediction.
record.rows_left_out: Main concept-erasure, adversarial-attack, and image-quality results in Tables 1–3 and other sections are omitted because they report model-level erasure outcomes, not evidence about the interpretability or explanatory sufficiency of the claim's neuron units.

record.verdict_notes: This is a diffusion-model concept-erasure paper built on SAE features. It measures no neuron-level interpretability shares and no explanation scoring, and there is no basis for any verdict on V1–V7. The reader's T4 / uses_without_test classification is sound, though a T6 reading would also be defensible, since the study relies on SAE features rather than the claim's neurons. Uncertainty estimates are absent. The kSAE has expansion factor 1 (1,280 latents).

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.4
rows.operation_detail: Measure directional ROC-AUC of selected kSAE features for distinguishing nudity from matched non-nudity prompts across denoising timesteps.
rows.measure: Directional ROC-AUC of selected kSAE features
rows.value: Mean AUC remains above 0.8 across denoising timesteps.
rows.note: The paper describes this as evidence that selected sparse features discriminate nudity from non-nudity prompts; it is not a test of neuron explanations in language models.
rows.check: Measures how well selected SAE features (not neurons) separate nudity from non-nudity prompts in a diffusion model. The features were chosen by contrasting the same kind of prompts, so this is close to a selection-validation value rather than an independent result. It bears on no version.
